issues.legal_issue: Minor discrepancies in recorded times do not by themselves render eyewitness testimony unreliable.
material_facts: The recorded times of the police message, the injured person's dispatch and arrival at the hospital were inconsistent by a short interval.
The records themselves indicated that the times could not all be exact, because the injured person could not have arrived at the hospital at the same time he was dispatched.
issues.conclusion: The discrepancy in timings was not a sufficient ground to reject the eyewitnesses' testimony.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the timing evidence in its full context and held that an apparent short timing discrepancy, where the recorded times were not necessarily accurate, did not make the eyewitness account false or doubtful. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.recorded_times_are_inconsistent: Different records or witnesses give inconsistent times for connected events.
predicates.records_show_times_are_approximate: The evidence indicates that the recorded times are not exact and cannot all be literally correct.

issues.definition: When an appeal against an acquittal involves inconsistent but evidently approximate recorded times, the eyewitness testimony is not rejected on that discrepancy alone.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of bloodstains on witnesses does not by itself disprove their account of an attack with bloodstained weapons.
material_facts: The witnesses said they had caught the assailants or taken weapons from them.
The weapons were bloodstained, but there was no proof that the witnesses' hands or clothes were bloodstained.
The court found no adequate basis to conclude that blood must have stained the witnesses during the incident.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness testimony could not be rejected because the witnesses had no proven bloodstains on their hands or clothing.
issues.legal_principle: Whether witnesses or their clothing would have been stained depended on the circumstances; the absence of proof of bloodstains did not disprove the prosecution account. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_against_acquittal and witnesses_handle_or_seize_weapons and weapons_are_bloodstained and not witness_bloodstains_proved

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.witnesses_handle_or_seize_weapons: Witnesses say they held an assailant or handled or seized a weapon during or after the incident.
predicates.weapons_are_bloodstained: The weapons connected to the incident are found to bear blood.
predicates.witness_bloodstains_proved: The witnesses' hands or clothing are shown to bear bloodstains.

issues.definition: In an appeal against an acquittal, handling weapons found to be bloodstained does not require rejection of eyewitness testimony when bloodstains on the witnesses themselves are not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A statement recorded after an investigation has begun cannot be relied on as the initial report, but its rejection in that capacity does not discredit eyewitness testimony assessed independently.
material_facts: The police had received information, attended the scene, sent the injured person to hospital, arrested an accused and seized clothing before recording the witness's statement.
The statement was recorded at the police station after those investigative steps had begun.
issues.conclusion: The statement could not be used as the initial report and was a statement recorded during investigation; rejecting it as the initial report did not detract from the eyewitnesses' testimony.
issues.legal_principle: A statement made to police after investigation has commenced is not the initial report and may be considered only as a statement recorded during investigation. The court separately assessed the eyewitness evidence on its merits. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.police_investigation_started_before_stat: Police had begun investigative steps concerning the occurrence before the statement was recorded.
predicates.statement_recorded_by_police: A witness's statement about the occurrence was recorded by police.

issues.definition: When police have begun investigating before recording a witness's statement, that statement is not usable as the initial report.

issues.legal_issue: Medical opinion about shock and speech does not conclusively exclude a dying declaration when other evidence supports the declarant's ability to speak at the time.
material_facts: Witnesses said the injured person named assailants shortly after the attack.

One doctor described the injured person as affected in speech and under shock when examined, while the doctor who conducted the post-mortem considered that he may have remained conscious and able to speak for some time.
The court found that the medical evidence did not rule out the possibility of speech immediately after the occurrence.
issues.conclusion: The possibility that the injured person made the reported dying declaration could not be ruled out, and the High Court was right to accept it.
issues.legal_principle: Medical opinion about later examination and the likely onset of shock is not conclusive about whether the injured person could speak immediately after being injured; the circumstances observed by witnesses are relevant to that assessment. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.witnesses_report_declaration_soon_after_: Witnesses say the injured person made a statement shortly after sustaining the injuries.
predicates.medical_opinion_does_not_exclude_speech: Medical evidence does not conclusively establish that the injured person could not speak at the time of the reported statement.

issues.definition: When witnesses report a statement soon after an injury and medical opinion does not exclude the ability to speak, the statement is not discarded as impossible.

issues.legal_issue: Defects in an identification parade do not require rejection of identification evidence independently supported by witnesses' direct observation of the accused during the incident.
material_facts: The prosecution did not establish adequate precautions to prevent witnesses from seeing the accused before the identification parade.
The evidence showed that the appellants were apprehended at the scene and that the witnesses had an opportunity to observe their features.
The second appellant was identified by most eyewitnesses at the parade; the court considered the parade evidence concerning the third accused unreliable.
issues.conclusion: The identification parade could not be given much weight in establishing the third accused's identity, but its defects did not justify rejecting the evidence concerning the appellants' participation, which was supported by the witnesses' opportunity to observe them at the scene.
issues.legal_principle: A flawed identification parade may warrant reduced reliance on parade identification, but it does not necessarily defeat identification supported by direct observation at the incident. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.identification_parade_precautions_unprov: The prosecution does not establish adequate precautions to prevent witnesses from seeing the suspects before a later identification parade.
predicates.witnesses_observed_accused_at_scene: Witnesses had an opportunity to observe the accused during the incident.

issues.definition: In an appeal against an acquittal, defects in a later identification parade do not defeat identification grounded in witnesses' observation of the accused during the incident.

issues.legal_issue: Independent and natural eyewitness testimony, reinforced by an immediate apprehension and production of an accused and recovery of bloodstained weapons, can sustain a murder conviction despite investigative shortcomings.
material_facts: The eyewitnesses lived near the scene, were independent of the parties and had no shown enmity toward either side.
The witnesses said they caught one accused at the scene and promptly handed him to police.
Weapons taken from the accused were found to bear human blood.
The injured person was reported to have named two assailants before dying.
The investigation had shortcomings, including missing station records and bloodstained clothing that did not reach the examiner; the court nonetheless assessed the remaining evidence and accepted it.
issues.conclusion: The combined evidence proved the appellants' complicity beyond reasonable doubt, and the conviction and sentence were affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The court accepted natural and independent eyewitness testimony where it was corroborated by the reported dying declaration, bloodstained weapons and immediate production of an accused before police. Investigative shortcomings did not require rejection of that evidence in the circumstances. The conviction was under section 302 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code; no earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: appeal_against_acquittal and independent_natural_eyewitnesses and (reported_dying_declaration or bloodstained_weapons_recovered or accused_promptly_produced_to_police)

predicates.appeal_against_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal against an acquittal.
predicates.independent_natural_eyewitnesses: Witnesses were naturally present near the incident and had no shown enmity or dependence that undermined their testimony.
predicates.reported_dying_declaration: Witnesses report that the injured person identified an assailant before dying.
predicates.bloodstained_weapons_recovered: Weapons connected to the incident are recovered or produced and found to bear blood.
predicates.accused_promptly_produced_to_police: An accused is apprehended in connection with the incident and promptly handed over to police.

issues.definition: In an appeal against an acquittal, independent natural eyewitness testimony reinforced by at least one of a reported dying declaration, bloodstained recovered weapons or prompt production of an accused can sustain a murder conviction.
